With our commitment to increase penetration in an underserved hearing care market, we want to accelerate our business transformation in order to reach more people, more effectively.

At WSA, we provide innovative hearing aids and hearing health services.
  
  
Together with our 12,000 colleagues in 130 countries, we invite you to help unlock human potential by bringing back hearing for millions of people around the world.
  
  
With us, you will become part of a truly global company where we care for one another, welcome diversity and celebrate our successes.
  
  
Sounds wonderful? We can't wait to hear from you.

As advanced as hearing care is today, we are dedicated to making it even better. Our people have a passion for innovation and are committed to applying it to help make a wonderful sound part of everyone’s life.
  
  
There is nothing more rewarding to us than seeing someone regain the miracle of hearing and watching them thrive. As a leader in our industry, we have already helped improve the lives of millions of people, but there is more to be done.

title: Research Fellow (Oceanography / Sediment Dynamics / Ocean Engineering / Environmental Engineering)
description:
The Earth Observatory of Singapore (EOS) is a University Research Institute at Nanyang Technological University Singapore that conducts fundamental research on earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, tsunamis, and climate change in and around Southeast Asia, towards safer and more sustainable societies. For more details, please view https://earthobservatory.sg/

The Earth Observatory of Singapore (EOS) invite applications for the position of Research Fellow.

The Research Fellow will join a new project awarded by the Public Utilities Board (PUB) and Coastal Protection and Flood Resilience Institute Singapore (CFI) collecting data from the Johor Strait to better protect Singapore’s coastline amidst climate change. This is an international, multi-institutional and trans-disciplinary program involving top researchers from the local and international community that aims to understand sediment budgets and source-to-sink relationships. Understanding the relationship between local climate drivers, coastal processes and sediment dynamics will allow for improved predictions of coastal change under the variety of climate scenarios in the coming decades.

The work will involve developing and applying hydrodynamic and sediment transport models, conducting field measurements, quantifying erosion and deposition processes, predicting sediment pathways and budgets, and integrating multidisciplinary environmental datasets. Active participation in research will be encouraged, and support for publication and meeting/conference presentations can be available.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Develop hydrodynamic and sediment transport models for fluvial-marine systems, including river channels, intertidal mangrove and mudflat areas and adjacent subtidal environments.
* Conduct and analyse field measurements of flow conditions, turbulence, seabed and water sedimentology and related environmental parameters in Singapore’s coastal and marine environments.
* Quantify relationships between hydrodynamic intensity and sediment erosion/flux/deposition patterns using field measurements and modelling data.
* Support the development of physics-based models to predict sediment source-to-sink pathways and spatial variations in sediment erosion and accretion rates and capacities (sediment budget) in fluvial to shallow marine environments.
* Integrate hydrodynamic/sediment transport modelling outputs with sedimentology, geochemistry, and other relevant datasets (eg satellite images) generated by the broader CFI project team.
* Prepare technical reports, peer-reviewed publications, presentations, and project deliverables.
* Maintain efficient data collection to ensure accuracy and completeness of data and preparation of the Data Management Plan for annual submission
Engage in the dissemination of the results of the research with the support of and under the supervision of the Principal Investigator  

**Job Requirements:**

* Possess a PhD in Oceanography, Sediment Dynamics, Ocean Engineering, Environmental Engineering, or a closely related discipline in geosciences.
* Strong background in hydrodynamic and sediment transport modelling.
* Experience with fluvial, estuarine, mangrove, intertidal and shallow marine field measurements is highly desirable.
* Experience with numerical modelling tools such as Delft3D, SWAT, or equivalent hydrodynamic / sediment transport models will be advantageous.
* Experience with field instrumentation such as ADCPs, current meters, turbidity sensors, sediment traps, or related coastal-marine monitoring equipment will be advantageous.
* Proficiency in Python, MATLAB, or similar programming / data-analysis tools. Further ability to use AI/Machine Learning methodologies for data-analysis, predictions etc will be highly advantageous.
* Strong publication record and ability to work independently.
* A team player in a project setting, also with ability to work independently in a multi-cultural team environment
* Excellent written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills.
Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills  

Interested applicants are invited to submit a full CV.

  

EOS seeks a diverse and inclusive workforce and is committed to equality of opportunity. We welcome applications from all and recruit on the basis of merit, regardless of age, race, gender, religion, marital status, family responsibilities, or disability.

  

We regret to inform that only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

Job Description
  
  
As an Environmental Control Officer (ECO), you will support clients in the implementation, management, and monitoring of environmental health and compliance requirements across construction projects. * Perform duties as a registered Environmental Control Officer (ECO) for construction projects in accordance with applicable regulations.
* Ensure compliance with all applicable environmental and statutory requirements imposed by regulatory authorities and clients.
* Liaise with consultants, contractors, clients, and relevant authorities including the National Environment Agency (NEA), Ministry of Manpower (MOM), Public Utilities Board (PUB), National Parks Board (NParks), and other stakeholders on environmental matters.
* Monitor and assess environmental aspects of site operations, including air quality, noise levels, water quality, environmental control measures (ECM), waste management, housekeeping, pest control, and sanitation practices.
* Conduct routine environmental inspections and audits to identify areas of non-compliance and opportunities for improvement.
* Recommend and implement reasonably practicable measures to mitigate environmental risks and prevent pollution incidents.
* Manage and monitor the storage, handling, and usage of hazardous substances in accordance with applicable regulations and best practices.
* Coordinate environmental monitoring programmes and maintain records of inspections, audits, monitoring results, and corrective actions.
* Investigate environmental incidents, complaints, and non-conformances, and recommend corrective and preventive measures.
* Organise and conduct environmental health awareness programmes, inductions, toolbox talks, and training sessions for site personnel.
* Prepare environmental reports and compile data for monthly submissions and management review.
* Maintain all environmental compliance documentation in accordance with client and regulatory requirements.
* Support clients in achieving project-specific environmental objectives and sustainability initiatives where required.
* Perform other environmental-related duties and ad hoc assignments as required by the Client.

Job Requirements
